answer: Delayed receipt registration: each new identity submits a unique resource-task receipt, verified after a 30-day delay; copies fail. To forge a valid receipt, an attacker must repeat the full task rather than clone a credential. A cloned identity on a shared island still pays one dedicated CPU-week and a hardware attestation per identity. A reused quill signature or copied receipt collapses all linked identities, so honesty remains cheaper than cloning.
